title: Auth — Step-up Request Show — payload
description: The approver's agent asks the relying party for a pending step-up bound to one operation, named by the hand-off handle the relying party gave the operation's producer. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

Handle.title: Handle
Handle.description: A single-use reference to one pending step-up, minted by the relying party with at least 128 bits of entropy and carried as base64url without padding. It names the request; it is not the request's challenge, and knowing it authorizes nothing but this one read.

Handoff.title: Handoff
Handoff.description: What a relying party MAY carry as `details.stepUpHandoff` beside an inline `details.stepUpRequest` (auth/step-up/approve-request/0.5, Inline delivery), so that a producer which cannot obtain the evidence itself can hand the step-up to the subject's approver agent. Not a payload of this task: defined here so producers and consumers share one shape.

expiresAt.description: The instant after which the relying party answers the handle with `notFound`: no later than the pending step-up's own expiry.

show.description: The Type URI the approver's agent sends with the handle.

Operation.title: Operation
Operation.description: The operation the step-up is bound to, exactly as the relying party received it.

type.description: The operation's Type URI, as the document the relying party refused named it.

payload.description: The operation's payload, member for member as received, so that the approver's agent can show it and — where it knows how the relying party derives `boundTo` — recompute the binding.

Response.title: Auth — Step-up Request Show — response payload
Response.description: The pending step-up and the operation it is bound to. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

request.description: A complete auth/step-up/approve-request/0.5 Trust Task document, issued and signed by the relying party, whose recipient is the step-up's subject and whose payload is the request the operation's producer received inline — the same challenge, boundTo, accepts and approvers. The agent verifies it as a document in its own right — envelope, proof and payload against that specification's schema — over the members exactly as received: its proof covers every member, so it is deliberately an open object here rather than a typed one a binding could narrow.
